answer: Oasis Access requires a timed yield that decays with each new identity claiming the same reward zone; the decay function ensures the marginal clone receives less than their registration cost over time. Orchard Decay taxes each identity a fraction of their past rewards when entering the system, so creating clones triggers a ripple that drains accumulated value faster than it can be replenished. The enforcement rule is simple: identities in the same region must share a diminishing return pool, and the first to claim full yield sets the baseline for all others.
